newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axa no comment on UAP provisions report.
newsitem.headline: Axa no comment on UAP provisions report.

text.p: French insurer Axa declined to comment on a Tuesday newspaper report that merger partner Union des Assurances de Paris (UAP) would post a 1996 loss of six to seven billion francs after a big provisioning exercise.
"The Axa group cannot comment. The accounts have not been adopted," am Axa spokeswoman said in response to a query from Reuters on the report in Les Echos newspaper.

Les Echos said that Axa, which owns more than 90 percent of UAP but will not complete the megamerger legally until later this year, planned to take advantage of a breathing space to clean up the UAP books before publication of the first merged group results for the 1997 financial year.
It said the impact would be on the merged Axa-UAP group's equity funds rather than the balance sheet.

The provisions would cover the life and group insurance arms among other things, as well as 400 million francs for Banque Worms, which had cost UAP 15 billion francs over the five preceding years, Les Echos said.
Big provisions were due to be made for UAP Vie life business and UAP collectives, the group insurance business and also for the deconsolidating of BNP, the paper said.
